codeReview.summary: Clean, well-scoped prompt-only fix that correctly aligns buildPrompt() JSON schema instructions with all 6 EvaluatorResultSchema fields. The diff is minimal (11 lines changed in the transport, 44 lines added in tests), strictly within scope (no schema modification), and the prompt guidance is precise — especially the explicit 'NOT 0-100' note for confidence which prevents a common LLM misinterpretation. The new test properly captures the prompt via mock spawner and asserts all 6 field names plus the confidence range notation. All 6 schema fields (passed, reasoning, suggestions, confidence, feedback, files_to_review) are correctly represented in the prompt with accurate type descriptions matching the Zod schema.

issues.description: The test only exercises the 'claude' engine path (prompt captured from -p flag). While buildPrompt() is engine-agnostic so the content is identical regardless, a second assertion block for engineName:'opencode' (where prompt is captured from options.stdin) would make the test more robust against future refactors that might diverge prompt assembly per engine.

Minor: the prompt says 'suggestions: string[]' as always-present, but EvaluatorResultSchema defines suggestions as z.array(z.string()).optional(). The LLM will return an empty array (which satisfies .optional()), so this is functionally correct and arguably better behavior — but it's a subtle discrepancy between what the prompt implies (required) and what the schema accepts (optional).

sharedStateObservations.observation: The EvaluatorResultSchema has a comment noting 'ADR spec uses reason; kept as reasoning for backward compat — intentional deviation'. This deliberate schema deviation from the ADR is documented only as a code comment in src/schemas/evaluator.ts. If future workers need to work with the evaluator schema, they might not discover this unless they read the source. Could be worth noting in AGENTS.md or library/architecture.md.
